scenario: AITA for telling my fiance we shouldn't get another bird after we lost ours last night? | Me and my fiance had a lovebird named Rosie. She was the sweetest little thing ever. Last night, she had suffered what we believe to be a sudden heart attack, and she passed away; we have literally no idea how it happened as she was very well taken care of, and she was perfectly fine earlier yesterday. Both of us are devastated right now and grieving, especially my fiance as she has been having severe depression the past few weeks, so this doesn't help her at all. We said our goodbyes, and let her Today as i am playing video games, i overhear her making phone calls to pet shops and animal shelters asking for birds they have. She called her aunt to ask for money to get another bird, so i tried to stop her saying "no we shouodn't, its a bad idea right now. We just lost Rosie last night" i was upset because not only did i find that not healthy, but i saw it as immediately replacing something we both loved. She got annoyed with me and told me it would help her feel better and to grieve. We argued back and forth for a bit. My fiance called me an asshole and said i have no say in the matter, which i feel as though i do because i pay the rent and bills in our apartment, money is super tight cause i am the only one working right now, and it would be my money that pays for this bird (we have separate accounts). At the moment, we are both upset and not talking. I never mentioned we should never get a pet ever again, i just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn, and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive to her cause she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not worse than i am, but i feel like i didnt do it right. Am i the asshole in this scenario? Thanks.

We're not talking right now, and I feel like I didn't handle the situation well. I don't think it's healthy to immediately replace Rosie, especially when we're both grieving. Plus, financially, we're tight because I'm the only one working right now. I don't want to add another expense when we're already struggling. But maybe I was too harsh. She's feeling the loss deeply, and getting another bird might help her cope. I should have been more understanding instead of just saying it's a bad idea. Maybe I should have suggested waiting a bit longer or finding other ways to help her feel better instead of outright saying no. I'm also thinking about our relationship. We're supposed to support each other, especially during tough times. By telling her no, I might have made her feel worse. She might have felt like I didn't care about her feelings or that I was being controlling. That's not how I want her to see me. On the other hand, I was trying to be responsible. We have financial constraints, and adding another pet could strain us further. Plus, I was worried about the emotional impact of replacing Rosie so quickly. I didn't want her to feel like we're just moving on without properly grieving. Maybe the problem was how I approached the situation. Instead of saying it was a bad idea, I could have expressed my concerns more gently. I could have acknowledged her pain and suggested that we wait a little while before making any decisions. That way, I'm still being supportive but also responsible. I also need to consider her perspective. She's dealing with depression and the loss of Rosie. Getting another bird might be her way of coping, even if it's not the healthiest. I should have been more empathetic and less focused on the practical aspects. Maybe I should have asked her how she feels about getting another bird and if she thinks it's the right decision for both of us. In the end, I think I was partly right in wanting to wait, but I was wrong in how I communicated it. I should have been more understanding and less confrontational.
